## Exercise 6: start from generic MLIR {#arithmetic-objective}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```bash
cat examples/ex6_arith_muli.mlir
```

<div class="code-gap"></div>

```mlir
module {
  func.func @ex6_mul(%a : i8, %b : i8) -> i8 {
    %r = arith.muli %a, %b : i8
    return %r : i8
  }
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
**Objective: a combinational hardware module**

```mlir
hw.module @ex6_mul(
    in %in0 : i8, in %in1 : i8, out out0 : i8) {
  %0 = comb.mul %in0, %in1 : i8
  hw.output %0 : i8
}
```

This is the smallest complete path to SystemVerilog and logic synthesis.
:::
:::
::::

## Exercise 6: find the missing passes - 3 min {#arithmetic-exercise-6}

To reach that objective, two things must change:

- `func.func` and `return` must become a hardware module boundary.
- `arith.muli` must become a combinational multiplier.

Does upstream `circt-opt` provide both transformations?

```bash
circt-opt --help | grep -i arith
circt-opt --help | grep -i func
```

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Relevant `arith` result**

```text
--convert-comb-to-arith
--lower-hwarith-to-hw
--map-arith-to-comb
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Relevant `func` result**

```text
--lower-cf-to-handshake
    Lower func and CF into Handshake IR
```

No direct generic `func.func` → `hw.module` pass.
:::
::::

## `map-arith-to-comb` draws a deliberate line {#arithmetic-map-contract}

```{.text code-line-numbers="2,4|5-6|9-13"}
def MapArithToCombPass : Pass<"map-arith-to-comb"> {
  let summary = "Map arith ops to combinational logic";
  let description = [{
    A pass which does a simple `arith` to `comb` mapping wherever possible.
    This pass will not convert:
    * floating point operations
    * operations using `vector`-typed values

    This does not intend to be the definitive lowering/HLS pass of `arith`
    operations in CIRCT (hence the name "map" instead of e.g. "lower").
    Rather, it provides a simple way (mostly for testing purposes) to map
    `arith` operations.
  }];
}
```

[CIRCT `Transforms/Passes.td`, pinned `firtool-1.147.0` source](https://github.com/llvm/circt/blob/firtool-1.147.0/include/circt/Transforms/Passes.td#L56-L76)

The failure is the documented boundary of the pass. Our exercise supplies one
concrete floating-point lowering.

## Eight bits encode several numerical regimes {#arithmetic-e4m3-format}

::: {.bit-layout}
::: {.bit-field .sign}
**s**

`[7]`

<small>sign · 1 bit</small>
:::
::: {.bit-field .exponent}
**eeee**

`[6:3]`

<small>biased exponent · 4 bits</small>
:::
::: {.bit-field .fraction}
**mmm**

`[2:0]`

<small>stored fraction · 3 bits</small>
:::
:::

| Regime | Encoding | Value |
|---|---|---|
| zero | `e = 0000`, `m = 000` | $0$ |
| subnormal | `e = 0000`, `m != 000` | $(-1)^s 2^{-6}(m/8)$ |
| normal | `e != 0000` | $(-1)^s 2^{e-7}(1+m/8)$ |
| NaN | `e = 1111`, `m = 111` | not a number |

`f8E4M3FN` has bias 7, finite values up to 448, and no infinity.
[@micikevicius2022fp8]

## Subnormals fill the gap around zero {#arithmetic-e4m3-axis}

![](assets/images/e4m3-number-line.svg){fig-alt="Positive E4M3FN values near zero, with subnormal and normal ranges distinguished" width="100%"}

| Bits | Hex | Value |
|---|---:|---:|
| `0 0000 001` | `0x01` | $2^{-9}$ = 0.001953125 |
| `0 0000 111` | `0x07` | $7 \times 2^{-9}$ = 0.013671875 |
| `0 0001 000` | `0x08` | $2^{-6}$ = 0.015625 |

The sign bit mirrors these points onto the negative axis.

## The same format spans tiny values to 448 {#arithmetic-e4m3-values}

| Hex | Fields `s eeee mmm` | Value |
|---:|---|---:|
| `0x00` | `0 0000 000` | 0 |
| `0x08` | `0 0001 000` | $2^{-6}$ |
| `0x30` | `0 0110 000` | 0.5 |
| `0x38` | `0 0111 000` | 1 |
| `0x3C` | `0 0111 100` | 1.5 |
| `0x41` | `0 1000 001` | 2.25 |
| `0x7E` | `0 1111 110` | 448 |
| `0x7F` | `0 1111 111` | NaN |

Less precision buys a smaller representation and more operations per watt;
the exact rounding and exceptional-value rules remain part of the contract.

## Exercise 7: replace the floating-point island {#arithmetic-pass-goal}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="Two E4M3 inputs above an empty vertical multiplier datapath and an eight-bit result">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-target.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>

::: {.e4m3-figure-caption}
Normal path adapted from [@dinechin2024asa, Fig. 11.7].
:::
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
```mlir
%af = arith.bitcast %a : i8 to f8E4M3FN
%bf = arith.bitcast %b : i8 to f8E4M3FN
%p = arith.mulf %af, %bf : f8E4M3FN
%r = arith.bitcast %p : f8E4M3FN to i8
```

Root the rewrite at the final `arith.bitcast`: the matched island and its
replacement then have the same `i8` boundary.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-target}
```python
def lower_e4m3_mul(out_cast, rewriter):
    matched = match_e4m3_island(out_cast)  # supplied
    if matched is None:
        return True
    lhs, rhs = matched
    with rewriter.ip:
        ...
    rewriter.replace_op(out_cast, [result])
    return False

patterns.add(
    arith.BitcastOp, lower_e4m3_mul)
```
:::
:::
::::

**Scope:** normal, finite, non-zero operands; normal result; no rounding yet.

## Together: route the sign {#arithmetic-sign-path}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier datapath">
  <img class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="0" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-target.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
**First make the rewrite compile.** Extract both signs, XOR them, and set the
remaining seven output bits to zero.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-sign .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
**Sign path**

```python
sa = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, lhs).result
sb = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, rhs).result
sign = comb.XorOp.create(sa, sb).result

zero7 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i7, 0).result
result = comb.ConcatOp.create(sign, zero7).result
```
:::

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
The long purple wire is now a real SSA value from both inputs to the packed
result.
:::
:::
::::

## Exercise 7A: multiply the significands - 6 min {#arithmetic-exercise-7a}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier with its sign path completed">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
For normal operands, materialize the hidden `1`, then preserve the full
four-by-four-bit product. `comb.mul` returns the operand width.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-significand .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
**Solution**

```python
fa = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, lhs).result
fb = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, rhs).result
one = hw.ConstantOp.create(i1, 1).result
ma4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fa).result
mb4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fb).result

zero4 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i4, 0).result
ma8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, ma4).result
mb8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, mb4).result
raw = comb.MulOp.create(ma8, mb8).result
```
:::
:::
::::

## One bit chooses the normalization {#arithmetic-normalization-bit}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier through the full significand product">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
Normal significands are in $[1,2)$, so their product is in $[1,4)$.

::: {.e4m3-normal-table}
| `%raw[7]` | Keep | Exponent |
|---:|---|---:|
| `0` | `%raw[6:3]` | `+ 0` |
| `1` | `%raw[7:4]` | `+ 1` |
:::

`1.100₂ × 1.100₂ = 10.010000₂`

For `0x3C × 0x3C`, `%raw[7] = 1`: shift once and increment the exponent to
obtain `0x41` ($2.25$).
:::
::::

## Exercise 7B: build the normalization mux - 7 min {#arithmetic-exercise-7b}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier before normalization">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-normalize.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
Use `%raw[7]` both as data and as control: it selects the normalized window and
later increments the exponent.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-normalize .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
**Solution**

```python
norm = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, raw).result
direct = comb.ExtractOp.create(3, i4, raw).result
shifted = comb.ExtractOp.create(4, i4, raw).result
mant = comb.MuxOp.create(norm, shifted, direct).result
frac = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, mant).result
```
:::
:::
::::

## Together: adjust the exponent {#arithmetic-exponent-path}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier before exponent adjustment">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-normalize.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-exponent.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
Add the stored exponents, remove one bias, then add the normalization bit.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-exponent .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
**Exponent path**

```python
ea = comb.ExtractOp.create(3, i4, lhs).result
eb = comb.ExtractOp.create(3, i4, rhs).result
zero1 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i1, 0).result
ea5 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero1, ea).result
eb5 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero1, eb).result

sum_ = comb.AddOp.create(ea5, eb5).result
bias = hw.ConstantOp.create(i5, 7).result
base = comb.SubOp.create(sum_, bias).result
norm5 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, norm).result
adjusted = comb.AddOp.create(base, norm5).result
exp = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i4, adjusted).result
```
:::
:::
::::

## Together: pack and replace {#arithmetic-normal-path}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="Complete normal-path E4M3 multiplier">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-normalize.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-exponent.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-pack.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy}
The final value has the same `i8` type as the output bitcast being replaced.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-pack .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
**Finish the callback**

```python
result = comb.ConcatOp.create(sign, exp, frac).result
rewriter.replace_op(out_cast, [result])
return False
```
:::

The floating-point island is dead; the greedy rewrite removes it.
:::
::::

## This checkpoint is intentionally incomplete {#arithmetic-special-cases}

| Excluded case | Hardware still required |
|---|---|
| discarded product bits | round to nearest, ties to even |
| zero or subnormal input | the hidden bit is not always `1` |
| subnormal result | gradual-underflow shift and rounding |
| exponent overflow | E4M3FN overflow behavior |
| NaN input | detect and return the NaN encoding |

The normal-path circuit should compile, but the exhaustive checker is expected
to expose these missing cases:

```bash
./scripts/test-e4m3-all.py --pass
```

The complete reference is `examples/ex7_e4m3fn_mul_reference.sv`.

## If time: specialize a squarer {#arithmetic-square-extension}

`examples/optional_e4m3fn_square.mlir` contains `%x * %x`.

- Match equal SSA operands.
- Decode `%x` once.
- Emit a dedicated significand squarer.
- Prove equivalence, then compare AIG nodes and depth.
